cues.text: Start with the Architecture template.
Draw a wall to hold the panel while we build it.
Place axis helpers at the base, one at each side of the panel.
The Window tool gives us a frame and glass in two clicks.
Good. Explode turns the window into plain geometry that hotspots can drive.
Delete the wall and clear the helpers, and we're left with the panel.
Make Object, then Edit Prototype. Hotspots are defined inside the object.
First the size handle. Place Hotspot on the panel's right corner, set to Stretch.
Now the multiplier: another hotspot on the grid in front, named Count, set to Multiply Linear.
Window-select the whole panel and attach it. This is what gets copied.
Pick Reference, one panel width back. That distance is the step between copies.
Back to Size: select the panel's right side and the Count hotspot too, then attach them.
Attaching Count means the copies will follow when the panel gets wider.
Nice. Finish Editing. That's the whole definition, with no code at all.
Select the panel, and both handles appear. Drag Size to make it wider.
Now pull back to see more, and drag Count along the grid. Each panel width adds a panel.
Wow! A whole curtain wall from one drag.
Move Copy it, and each copy keeps its own size and count.
Drag this one back to three panels. The first doesn't change.
That's a dynamic object with no code: one size handle and one multiply handle.
